Part 1 · Scenarios

Which case sets each relief load?

Part 1 · the plan

Every credible case, one governing

API 521 asks for every cause of overpressure; the largest credible load sizes the valve.

  1. The scenario tableblocked outlet, fire, back-pressure, valve failure, blow-through
  2. The simulator runsSIS disabled and active

Scenarios · interactive

Pick a PSV

Blocked outlet governs every vessel: 8.9 / 18.6 / 8.4 / 9.4 t/h; fire never does.

Blocked outlet · interactive

Alarm, trip, relief: in what order?

With the SIS active, V-201..203 never lift; V-204 still lifts after PSHH-248: the cascade keeps feeding it.

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • Blocked outlet governs; V-201 cannot flash at 1.1 × set.
  • PSHH trips 1.3–8 min before the PSV set.
  • EQ-er-1: V-204 lifts after the trip; close LCV-231 or size for it.
2

Part 2 · Sizing

How big must each PSV orifice be?

Part 2 · the plan

Area, letter, inlet, outlet

The load gives an area; API 526 gives the next letter up; the piping must not starve or choke it.

  1. The sizing calculatorAPI 520 vapour equation
  2. The four PSVsG, J, J, K

API 520 · interactive

From relief load to orifice letter

$$A=\frac{W}{C\,K_d\,P_1}\sqrt{\frac{T Z}{M}}$$

$W$: load, kg/h; $P_1$: relieving pressure, kPa a; $T$: K; $Z$, $M$: compressibility, molar mass.

A required, mm²
orifice
rated, t/h

Higher set pressure, smaller orifice: the same 18.6 t/h needs J at 40 bar a.

Sizing · interactive

The four valves as sized

1½G3, 3J4, 3J4, 3K4: inlet loss under 3 %, built-up back-pressure under 10 %.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • A required 292 / 826 / 526 / 1056 mm² → G / J / J / K.
  • PSV-227 and 237 inlets stepped to 3" to keep the 3 % rule.
  • Bellows valves against the flare back-pressure.
3

Part 3 · Flare and thermal relief

What must the header take?

Part 3 · the plan

Credible simultaneity, trapped liquid

The flare is sized for what can happen together, not for every valve at once.

  1. The flare basissingle, simulated, summed
  2. Thermal reliefa blocked-in product line warming up

Flare · interactive

Which load sizes the header?

The largest simultaneous lift in any run is 19.1 t/h: the sum of all rated flows, 52.9 t/h, is not credible.

Thermal relief · interactive

A blocked-in product line warming up

$$\frac{dP}{dT}=\frac{\beta}{\kappa},\quad q=\beta\,V\,\frac{dT}{dt}$$

$\beta$: expansion, 1/K; $\kappa$: compressibility, 1/bar; $V$: trapped volume.

relief flow, L/h
bar per °C if blocked

Only 74 L/h at 1 °C/min, but 14.7 bar per °C if nothing relieves: TSV-256 is small and essential.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Flare basis 19.1 t/h (simulated), header 1.5 bar a, DN300 assumed.
  • Depressuring not applicable: an aqueous system.
  • A thermal relief valve protects the blocked-in product line.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

List every scenario; the largest credible load governs.

2

The SIS trips first; the PSV is the last layer.

3

A trip that stops the feed may not stop the inflow.

4

Area → API 526 letter → inlet and outlet checks.

5

Size the flare on credible simultaneity.
